statement: Page 11, Graph 4 reports a small consecutive-line repetition peak in the English control, Dryden’s translation of the Aeneid. The English curve flattens after that peak, whereas the Voynich curve continues declining with line distance. The two controls are the Latin Aeneid and its English verse translation. Page 24, Graph 12 compares particular od/ed spellings: the listed od variants occur across the manuscript, while their matched ed forms are absent on Currier A pages in the analysis. The chronology on page 25 depends on Timm's proposed mechanism introducing those variants during production. A general A/B inventory asymmetry would be broader than the published evidence. The summary is right to report the chronology as the author's argument and to distinguish the observations from a validated generator. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.6639v3
